content.title: The Masters 2026: Rory McIlroy repeats as champion, first to go back-to-back since Tiger Woods
content.text: Rory McIlroy joined a select circle of four as back-to-back Masters champions on Sunday (12 April), when the Northern Irishman held off world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler by a single stroke for victory. McIlroy became the first repeat men's champion at Augusta since Tiger Woods pulled off the feat in 2001-02. Jack Nicklaus and Nick Faldo are the others in the highly exclusive club. In the year's first golf major, McIlroy posted a 71 in the final round for a 12-under 276 total. He led or co-led after each round. Needing more than a decade to win his first green jacket last year to complete the career Grand Slam, the 36-year-old only had to wait a year to pick up his second. "I thought it was so difficult to win last year because of trying to win the Masters and the grand slam," McIlroy said. "And then this year, I realized it's just really difficult to win the Masters. I tried to convince myself it was both." Three-time runner-up Justin Rose, who was bidding to become the second-oldest champion at 45, finished for a share of third place at 10 under with Tyrrell Hatton, Russell Henley, and Cameron Young. Rose had a two-shot lead going into the second nine but squandered his advantage with four bogeys as McIlroy - who Rose lost to in a play-off last year - tightened the screws down the stretch. McIlroy bogeyed the 18th but held on, and held off Paris 2024 Olympic gold medallist Scheffler, who fired a 68 on the final day to become the first golfer since World War II to play without a bogey over the last two rounds at the Masters. McIlroy now has six major championships, tied with Faldo for second most by a European golfer. Only Harry Vardon of England has seven. "I don't make it easy," said McIlroy, whose 73 in the previous round had allowed Young to move into a tie for first. "I used to make it easy back in my early 20s when I was winning these things by eight shots. It's just hard. It's hard to win golf tournaments." 2026 Masters Tournament: All results and scores - full list
